question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\log{\left(x \right)}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\log{\left(x \right)}}{7 x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}\int \log{\left(x \right)}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot \frac{u^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{u^{2}}{14}+C \\  & =\frac{\log{\left(x \right)}^{2}}{14}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\log{\left(x \right)}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{9}{x\sqrt{\log{\left(x \right)}}}\,\text{d}x & =9\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{\log{\left(x \right)}}}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =9\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =9\int u^{- \frac{1}{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =9\cdot \frac{u^{\frac{1}{2}}}{\frac{1}{2}}+C \\  & =18 \sqrt{\log{\left(x \right)}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\log{\left(x^{4} \right)}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x^{4}}\cdot 4 x^{3}=\frac{4}{x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac{1}{4}\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$

$$
